152	## Resource supply and feasibility
153	
154	The `carbon_market.resources` module complements job acceptance with a persistent, versioned resource-supply registry and a feasibility query over it. `resources.publish(path, resource, idempotency_key)` publishes one supply version: the resource object carries exactly `resource_id`, `region`, `capacity`, `start`, `end`, `unit_cost`, `carbon_intensity` and `residency` — non-empty id and region strings, a positive integer capacity, non-boolean non-negative start, end, unit cost and carbon intensity with start not later than end, and a residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted by code point that contains the resource's own region. A first publication returns the canonical record — the resource fields plus the next consecutive `version` for that resource id — with `True`, and atomically commits the record, the idempotency binding and a publish audit event binding key, resource id and version. Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the stored record with `False` and writes nothing; the same key with a different resource, or a new version whose start does not strictly increase over the resource's current latest, raises `ValueError`.
155	
156	`resources.get(path, resource_id, version=None)` reads one record back: the latest version when `version` is omitted, otherwise the exact version. An unknown resource id or version raises `KeyError`.
157	
158	`resources.feasible(job_path, supply_path, job_id, at)` joins a `jobs.submit` acceptance file with the supply file — both read as complete snapshots while their shared locks are held together — and ranks the resources that can serve job `job_id` at the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at`. Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at `at`; a candidate must sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as capacity, cover the job's residency regions, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total carbon the work times the carbon intensity; exceeding either budget excludes the candidate. The result is ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each entry carrying the resource record and both totals — an empty list when nothing qualifies. A version-1 `jobs.register` file is invalid structure here, and an unknown job id raises `KeyError`.
159	
160	The supply file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document — version, history sorted by resource id and version, idempotency map sorted by key, audit events — with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline; negative-zero and non-finite number literals are illegal. Every read entry (`publish`, `get` and `feasible`, and any consumer of the supply file) requires the on-disk bytes to be exactly that canonical form: a file whose fields or keys are out of order, which carries any whitespace beyond the structural tokens, which escapes non-ASCII characters, or which misses or doubles the final newline is rejected with `ValueError` just like a malformed or structurally invalid file. Publishing commits under the per-real-path cross-process exclusive lock with pre-call byte restoration on commit failure, queries take the shared lock, and invalid arguments, values, encodings, JSON, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references raise `ValueError`, missing input files or publish parent directories `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`.
161	
162	## Market clearing
163	
164	The `carbon_market.market.clear(jobs, supply, ledger, job_id, key, at)` entry adds the new-market clearing ledger on top of accepted jobs and the versioned resource supply. The three paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings, `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment, and the three paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before any business file is read.
165	
166	The acceptance file and the supply file are read as one snapshot under their shared locks, together with the ledger's exclusive lock; the three locks are taken in resolved real-path sorted order so concurrent calls can never deadlock. Only each resource's highest version valid at `at` is considered, and region, residency, cost budget, carbon budget, deadline coverage and the candidate entries (`resource`, `total_cost`, `total_carbon`) follow exactly the `resources.feasible` semantics. In addition, each resource version's capacity is reduced by the work of every trade already booked against that exact resource version in the ledger, so concurrent clearings can never oversell capacity and bookings never cross resource versions. The remaining candidates are ordered by carbon intensity, unit cost and resource id; the first one is the unique winner.
167	
168	The call returns `(trade, created)`. The trade binds the job id, the evaluation moment, the work, the complete ordered candidate snapshot and a versioned selection (`resource_id`, `version`). A missing ledger is created only when the first trade is made; the trade, the idempotency binding (key to job id and evaluation moment) and the audit event binding the request key, the resource id and its selected version are committed together — ledger sections sorted by code point, compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline, written through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the pre-call bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist).
169	
170	Replaying the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade with `False` without reselecting a resource, appending an event or rewriting a byte. The same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another idempotency key, raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger byte-for-byte untouched. An unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource raises `LookupError`; neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError` without leaving a ledger or temporary fragment. Invalid ledger structure, references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing `market.match`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.
171	
172	## Dispatch commitments
173	
174	The `carbon_market.dispatch` module adds the scheduling-commitment layer on top of the clearing ledger, with four persistent, idempotent calls over one dispatch ledger (`version`, `decisions` sorted by job id, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).
175	
176	`dispatch.commit(jobs, supply, trades, ledger, job_id, key, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file and the clearing ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock, all four taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the job's decision: it binds the traded resource id and version and the job's deadline, and starts `ready` with zero attempts and no owner or lease. The dispatch ledger is created only by this first commit. An unknown job raises `KeyError`, a job without a recorded trade `LookupError`, and a commit moment past the job's deadline `TimeoutError`.
177	
178	`dispatch.claim(ledger, job_id, key, owner, lease, at)` moves a `ready` or `failed` decision to `claimed` under a non-empty owner with a positive integer lease, counting one more attempt; the lease ends at `at + lease` and may not pass the job's deadline. A decision still held under a valid lease, or a lease end beyond the deadline, raises `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.finish(ledger, job_id, key, owner, result, at)` lets the current owner inside its lease record `succeeded` or `failed` and clears owner and lease; a non-claimed decision or an illegal result raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.recover(ledger, job_id, key, at)` returns a decision whose lease has strictly expired to `ready` without counting an attempt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These three actions take only the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.
179	
180	All four calls return `(decision, created)`; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current decision with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, owner, result, moment or lease raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the decision, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed decision snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure, so no failed call leaves a half-state. Invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, the reservation migration, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.
181	
182	## Execution plans
183	
184	The `carbon_market.execution` module adds the recoverable execution layer on top of the dispatch ledger, with three persistent, idempotent calls over one execution ledger (`version`, `plans` keyed by job id and dispatch attempt, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).
185	
186	`execution.plan(jobs, supply, trades, dispatch, ledger, job_id, key, owner, source, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file, the clearing ledger and the dispatch ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the execution ledger's exclusive lock, all five taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the plan for one `claimed` decision held by `owner` and still inside its lease — a decision in any other state raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. The plan is numbered by the decision's dispatch attempt count and fixes the job, the traded resource id and version, the deadline, the owner and the lease end; one dispatch attempt yields at most one plan. An empty `source` (`None` or `""`) creates a `launch` plan whose steps are `stage` then `start`; a non-empty `source` creates a `migrate` plan whose steps are `copy` then `switch`, and the source must name a published resource other than the target whose residency list covers the job's residency regions, else `LookupError`. A job without a recorded trade raises `LookupError` as well, and an unknown job or decision `KeyError`. The execution ledger is created only by this first plan.
187	
188	`execution.record(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, owner, step, result, receipt, at)` appends one step receipt — the step, `succeeded` or `failed`, a non-empty receipt string and the moment — to an active plan; steps advance only on success, a receipt naming anything but the next pending step raises `ValueError`, a failed step terminates the plan as `failed`, a successful last step as `completed`, and terminal plans accept no further receipts. Only the plan's owner acting inside the lease may record: a different owner raises `PermissionError` and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `execution.recover(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, at)` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired `interrupted`, preserving every recorded receipt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These two calls take only the execution ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.
189	
190	All three calls return `(plan, created)` and share one idempotency key space; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current plan with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, attempt, owner, source, step, result, receipt or moment raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the plan, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed plan snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure. An unknown job or attempt raises `KeyError`; invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `dispatch` interfaces, `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

192	## Execution synchronization
193	
194	The `carbon_market.execution_sync` module adds the persistent reconciliation layer on top of the execution and dispatch ledgers with one call, `execution_sync.run(execution, dispatch, ledger, owner, key, now, lease)`. The three ledger paths must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `owner` and `key` non-empty strings, `now` a non-boolean non-negative integer moment and `lease` a non-boolean positive integer coordination lease; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.
195	
196	The first call for a batch `key` scans the execution ledger by job id and attempt and fixes the batch as exactly the terminal plans (`completed`, `failed` or `interrupted`) no earlier batch has already synced. A `completed` plan finishes the dispatch decision as succeeded, a `failed` plan as failed, and an `interrupted` plan recovers the strictly expired claim; the action moment is always history — the last step receipt's moment for a finish, the recorded execution-recovery moment for a recover — and a retry can never rewrite it. Each item is first persisted `pending` in the coordination ledger, and only then is the existing `dispatch.finish`/`dispatch.recover` interface called with an idempotency key derived stably from the batch key and the plan identity, so a crash re-entry replays the very same request. The item becomes `applied` only after a successful call or an equivalent replay, saving the returned decision; a failure records the public exception class, keeps the item pending and re-raises the original exception with its chain.
197	
198	The call returns `(batch, created)`, a fixed-order copy of the current batch snapshot and the first-creation flag. The same batch key fixes its first scan forever: re-entry continues the unfinished items and a completed batch replays without rewriting a byte; terminal plans appearing later require a new batch key, and even an empty first scan commits an explicit `completed` state with the full audit snapshot. An active batch may only be continued by its current owner — a different owner before strict lease expiry raises `PermissionError` — while after expiry another owner may take over without repeating any applied item. Before any advance, the dispatch decision's state, attempt, owner and lease are checked against the plan (as is a dispatch idempotency key already bound to a different request); any mismatch raises `ValueError` without advancing.
199	
200	The coordination ledger (`version`, `batches` sorted by key with each batch's items sorted, and an append-only `audit`) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. The coordination ledger's exclusive lock is taken first and held for the whole run, followed by the two input ledgers' shared locks in resolved real-path order — released before the existing dispatch interface takes the dispatch ledger's own exclusive lock per item — so concurrent processes lock in one acyclic real-path order and can never deadlock. Every commit goes through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the previous bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist) and clears the leftover fragment. Invalid structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; missing input files or the ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`; other locking or I/O failures raise `OSError`. The existing `execution`, `dispatch` and `market` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.
201	
202	## Live signal ledger
203	
204	The `carbon_market.signals` module adds an independent ledger of live signals beside the static cost and carbon intensity baked into a resource version. A signal carries exactly `region`, `observed`, `expires`, `mix`, `unit_cost` and `carbon_intensity` — a non-empty region string, non-boolean non-negative observation and expiration moments with the expiration not earlier than the observation, non-negative unit cost and carbon intensity, and a non-empty `mix` object whose values are non-negative integers summing to exactly ten thousand (basis points). Any extra field is rejected.
205	
206	`signals.publish(path, signal, idempotency_key)` publishes one signal version for its region. A first publication returns the canonical record — the signal fields plus the next consecutive `version` for that region, starting at 1 — with `True`, atomically committing the record, the idempotency binding and a publish audit event binding key, region and version. Replaying the same key with an identical signal returns the stored record with `False` and writes nothing; the same key with a different signal, or a new version whose `observed` does not strictly increase over the region's current latest, raises `ValueError` and preserves the original bytes.
207	
208	`signals.get(path, region, at)` returns the region's latest signal observed no later than the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at` and not expired at it (when several windows cover `at`, the highest version wins). An unknown region raises `KeyError`, and no valid version raises `LookupError`.
209	
210	The signal file follows the supply file's exact contract: one compact UTF-8 JSON document — version, history sorted by region and version, idempotency map sorted by key, audit events — with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals and exactly one trailing newline, and every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form. Publishing takes the per-real-path cross-process exclusive lock with pre-call byte restoration on commit failure; invalid arguments, values, encodings, JSON, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references raise `ValueError`, a missing input file or publish parent `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`.
211	
212	## Live feasibility and clearing
213	
214	`resources.feasible_live(job_path, supply_path, signal_path, job_id, at)` is the dynamic counterpart of `resources.feasible`: the acceptance, supply and signal files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks (the three paths must be distinct real locations). Each resource contributes only its highest supply version valid at `at`; its region, capacity, residency and deadline constraints are unchanged, but the unit cost and carbon intensity are taken from the resource region's latest signal that is valid at `at` rather than from the supply version. A region without a current signal simply removes that resource; it is never an error. The totals, `max_cost`/`carbon_cap` exclusions and the ordering (signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id) follow `feasible`; each result entry carries `resource`, `signal` (the full frozen signal record with its version), `total_cost` and `total_carbon`, and an empty list means no candidate. An unknown job raises `KeyError`.
215	
216	`market.clear_live(jobs, supply, signals, ledger, job_id, key, at)` adds live clearing on top of the same clearing ledger used by `market.clear` — the call takes the three snapshot shared locks and the ledger exclusive lock, all four locked in resolved real-path order, and deducts each booking from the capacity of the exact resource version, counting trades made by either `clear` or `clear_live`, so the two pricing modes share one capacity pool and never oversell. Feasibility follows `resources.feasible_live`: highest valid supply version, latest unexpired region signal driving cost and carbon, the same residency, budget, deadline and ordering rules. The returned trade freezes the ordered candidates, each carrying both its immutable resource version and its immutable signal version, and the selection keeps `resource_id` and `version`; a signal published after the trade can never change it.
217	
218	The replay and conflict rules mirror `clear`: the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade — static or live — with `False` without reselecting, appending an event or rewriting a byte; the same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another key, raises `ValueError` with the ledger untouched; an unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource `LookupError`, neither creating the ledger. The ledger keeps the same version 2 canonical form; static trades stay signal-free while live trades carry the frozen signal, so existing `clear`, `dispatch`, `execution` and `execution_sync` readers keep working over a ledger that contains live trades. Invalid structure, references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing resource, clearing and README public entry points and the HTTP behavior are unchanged.
219	
220	## Re-evaluation and migration advice
221	
222	The `carbon_market.rebalance` module adds the missing re-evaluation layer on top of the live signals, the booked clearing trades and the dispatch and execution layers. `rebalance.evaluate(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, ledger, job_id, key, at)` re-reads an unfinished booking at the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at` and advises whether the job should keep running on the resource version its trade froze or migrate to a resource whose current version is cleaner or cheaper under the latest signals. The seven paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings and the seven paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.
223	
224	All seven files are read as one snapshot: the six input files under shared locks and the advice ledger under its exclusive lock, all taken in resolved real-path order. The retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade froze — a newer published version of the same resource never replaces it, even once the frozen version's own supply window would have passed. A migration item uses only another resource's highest supply version valid at `at`, never a different version of the current resource. Every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later than `at` and not expired at it (a region without such a signal simply drops out), and keeps the job's regions, residency, deadline coverage, cost budget and carbon budget. Capacity is deducted per exact resource version for the trades of every *other* job, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never deducted against itself. Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id. The first item is the advice target: `keep` when it is still the current resource version, otherwise `migrate`.
225	
226	Advice is refused before any write, in a fixed order: a dispatch decision that has already succeeded, or an execution plan that has already completed, raises `ValueError`; an active execution plan raises `PermissionError` (the booking must not be re-decided while work is in flight); and an evaluation moment past the job deadline raises `TimeoutError`. An unknown job or dispatch decision raises `KeyError`; a job without a recorded trade or an empty feasible set raises `LookupError`; none of these creates the advice ledger. An interrupted or failed plan does not block re-evaluation; the record's `execution` field freezes `none`, `active`, `completed`, `failed` or `interrupted` from the plan with the highest dispatch attempt, and `dispatch` freezes the decision state at evaluation time.
227	
228	The call returns `(record, created)`. The record freezes, in order, `job_id`, `at`, `current` (`resource_id`/`version`), the `dispatch` and `execution` states, the ordered `candidates` (each carrying the frozen resource record, the frozen signal record, `total_cost` and `total_carbon`), the `recommendation` and the `target`. A first evaluation returns the record with `True` and commits it together with one audit event in the advice ledger; replaying the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored record with `False` without writing a byte, while the same key with a changed request raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger untouched.
229	
230	The advice ledger (`version`, `records` and `audit` sorted by idempotency key) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form; the frozen supply and signal references, totals, ordering, the current selection and the keep/migrate target are revalidated against the current snapshots, while the dispatch/execution states stay frozen point-in-time facts. Commits go through a synced same-directory temporary file, an atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on failure; a failed call leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit event, and a missing ledger parent raises `FileNotFoundError` without creating the ledger. Invalid arguments or ledger bytes raise `ValueError`, other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `resources`, `market`, `dispatch`, `execution` and `execution_sync` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.
231	
232	## Advice execution and re-reservation
233	
234	`rebalance.apply(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, job_id, advice_key, key, at)` turns one recorded migration advice into a persisted re-reservation, so the target capacity the advice pointed at is pre-emptively held for the job before any execution plan moves it. The eight paths — the seven snapshots of `evaluate` plus the intent ledger — must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `job_id`, `advice_key` and `key` must be non-empty strings and `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer reservation moment; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.
235
